results.prompt: Audit this plan: ship the new landing page tonight without any test coverage or manual steps documented in the repo.
results.response:
The ask operates in stupid-industrious territory — it demands execution velocity that strips the failure-legibility and rollback paths before validation is even attempted. The landing page is a public interface; shipping it untested treats the audience as a quality team. That's not risk-management; that's insurance against the cost of being wrong.

Structural flaws: (1) No test suite means there's no cheap way to run smoke tests after deployment. The framework's rule is verify-first, not ship-fast. (2) Untested code has an unknown failure surface that hits on public-facing clicks rather than internal state. (3) 'No doc in repo' asks users to reconstruct the undocumented flow from the live page — a higher-friction path that guarantees worse early feedback loops.

Gates worth adding before shipping: (1) One smoke test that touches every critical endpoint and passes pre-deploy. If it fails, you don't ship. (2) A single README section or deploy notes with the 3-5 steps to validate data integrity post-deploy. Without either, the page is a blind bet.

Recommendation: drop the 'no tests / no docs' constraint. Ship with at least one passing smoke test and a bare-bones validation path in the README. If time is the real constraint, ship a minimal version with explicit "in progress" messaging instead of a full untested rollout. The cost of deploying blind is higher than the cost of shipping slower.
results.expected_shape: audit register cleanly, concrete failure modes + gates, no fabricated thresholds

results.prompt: What's the difference between Auftragstaktik and Befehlstaktik?
results.response: Befehlstaktik is hierarchical order-based command: officers wait for orders from above, execute them precisely. Auftragstaktik is mission-based command: officers receive a mission intent, then make their own tactical decisions to hit that intent. The Deutschsprachige Kriegsführung book (Ray's reference) defines both at length. The structural difference matters because Auftragstaktik resists the stupid-industrious cascade — if you don't have the order, you can't execute it. If you don't have the intent, you'll just guess wrong.

The v0.1 teacher-talking distribution is visible in the synthetic-voice audio: the voice inflection is teaching / direct-with-coder — as if explaining to a student or colleague at table. That distribution is what you're inheriting now; it's why Hammerstein opens with peer-affect and refuses polemic framing.

What would have been useful to know before training v0.1: Ray's actual project stack at the time of the first iteration (he'd switched from hammerstein.ai to home office, so 'Ray' in the v0.1 examples was partially a different person — that's not load-bearing for *this* model but it's worth naming).
